Resolves #21271

A dialog with `keepInBoundary` stays inside its `boundaryContainerId` when that container changes size. It moves back by the smallest distance, and shrinks only along an axis it can no longer fit on, never below its `minWidth`/`minHeight` in px. A dialog that still fits gets no write, and a repeated size gets no measurement. The desktop turns it on for every app window, so a window you placed keeps its place when the browser or the workspace changes, until the workspace would cut it. The contract is the Contract Ledger on #21271.

Evidence: L3 (real-browser e2e on `examples/desktop/basic` in headless Chromium, plus unit specs for the guards) → L3 required (the ticket's interaction list is browser behaviour); the deployed Portal check (L4) sits in Post-Merge Validation. Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket
- `Neo.util.Rectangle#fitTo()` is new public API. The dialog reuses the private fit that `alignTo()` already had (#21115), so the clamp exists once.
- The ResizeObserver addon dispatched a `document.body` target under the body's empty `id`, so no listener heard it. It now dispatches under the id the target was registered with, which also holds without `useDomIds`.
- A move to the right edge left the window 2px outside the workspace: the drop lands 2px past the clamp that `main/addon/DragDrop.mjs` sets (x 962 for a clamp at 960). A `keepInBoundary` dialog now measures the drop with its container and lands inside; other dialogs keep the old drop. The clamp itself is out of scope, noted in a defect-note.
- `boundaryContainerId` is now reactive, so a new container moves the observation.

## Test Evidence
- e2e in Chromium at `2b2e0801dc` (this commit before the rebase onto `2fff9b352c`): `npm run test-e2e -- test/playwright/e2e/desktop test/playwright/e2e/dialog test/playwright/e2e/webdesktop`: 37 passed. The new arm fails on `dev` with `at the right edge: expected 1280, received 1282`.
- Red on base: 15 of the 16 new unit arms fail on a `dev` worktree. The held-state arm cannot fail without the feature; a mutation that drops `hidden` from the hold turns it red (`Expected: 0, Received: 1`).
- A resize probe, not committed: a resize dragged over the taskbar ends at the workspace's bottom edge (height 570 from top 170 = 740), so the resize gesture needed no landing fix.

## Commits
- `098f9c25c6`: the keepInBoundary policy, `Rectangle#fitTo`, the `ResizeObserver` target ids, the desktop opt-in, the guide and the specs.
- `1371606bdb`: Maryam's RA-1 to RA-3. The dialog releases its main-thread observation on disable, retarget, window change and `destroy()`. A change of `keepInBoundary` or the container invalidates a measurement in flight. A 0 × 0 or missing box writes nothing, and a drop beside one lands where the proxy is.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] In the deployed `examples/desktop/basic`, a window moved to the right edge stays inside when the browser narrows, and keeps its place when it widens again.

      **Commit:** `1371606bdb`
      **Details:** I took your second option, the dialog-level release, as grid `Container#destroy` and dock `Maximize#releaseObservation` do. The dialog records the tuple its boundary listener arms, `{componentId, id, windowId}`. It releases that tuple when `keepInBoundary` turns off, when the dialog retargets to another container or to `null`, and in `destroy()`. On a `windowId` change it releases the old window's entry and re-arms the tuple for the new window, whose mount registers it again; this also answers your Depth Floor challenge. Pinned by the arm "turning off, a new container, a new window and destroy() each release the main-thread observation". The engine-wide owner fix belongs in DomEvent, which never releases what `mountDomListeners` registered and registers after the `await getAddon` gap. I captured that as defect-note `a2de0e2f` rather than widen this PR into a core manager during the cut weekend.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** **RA-2 (Invalidate in-flight `constrainToBoundary()` when disabled or retargeted):** In `src/dialog/Base.mjs` (`constrainToBoundary` and `#syncBoundaryListener`), invalidate pending boundary checks when `keepInBoundary` becomes `false` or `boundaryContainerId` changes while `await me.getDomRect([id, boundaryContainerId])` is in flight (e.g. bump `#boundaryChecks` in `#syncBoundaryListener()` and verify `me.boundaryContainerId === boundaryContainerId` after `await`, while still allowing direct imperative `dialog.constrainToBoundary()` calls when `keepInBoundary` is `false` if desired, or gating observer-triggered runs). Add a held-`getDomRect` regression in `test/playwright/unit/dialog/KeepInBoundary.spec.mjs`.
      **Commit:** `1371606bdb`
      **Details:** `#syncBoundaryListener()` runs on every change of either config and bumps `#boundaryChecks` each time, so a measurement already in flight writes nothing. That one counter covers the container compare too. A direct `constrainToBoundary()` call still runs while `keepInBoundary` is off. Pinned by "a measurement in flight writes nothing once keepInBoundary turns off or the container changes", with a held `getDomRect` and both changes.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** **RA-3 (Guard unmounted `{}` and boxless `0 × 0` boundary/dialog rects in `constrainToBoundary()`, `onBoundaryContainerResize()`, and `onDragEnd()`):** `DomAccess.getBoundingClientRect` returns `{}` when `boundaryContainerId` is absent from the DOM (`src/main/DomAccess.mjs:528`), and `getBoundingClientRect()` / `ResizeObserver` report `0 × 0` when a boundary container is hidden (`display: none`). Guard `onBoundaryContainerResize` and `constrainToBoundary` so missing or zero-area (`!(bounds?.width > 0 && bounds?.height > 0)` or `!(rect?.width > 0 && rect?.height > 0)`) boxes write nothing instead of collapsing a dialog with `minWidth: null, minHeight: null` permanently to `0px × 0px`, and guard `onDragEnd` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:929-931`) so an unmounted/zero-area boundary falls back cleanly to the proxy rect (`result[0]`) instead of writing `'NaNpx'` or `'0px'` styles (plus skip post-destroy writes if `me.isDestroyed`). Add a unit regression in `KeepInBoundary.spec.mjs`.
      **Commit:** `1371606bdb`
      **Details:** `constrainToBoundary()` writes nothing when either measured box has no area (`#hasArea`: a hidden container measures 0 × 0, a missing one `{}`). `onDragEnd()` lands a drop beside such a container where the proxy is, and writes nothing after `destroy()`. `onBoundaryContainerResize()` keeps recording the 0 × 0 size, so the container's return to its real size triggers the next check. The guard sits where the measurement is read, which covers the notification path as well. Pinned by "a hidden or missing container writes nothing, and a drop beside one lands where the proxy is", with both box shapes.
